subject: economics
title: Market Structures
welcome_lead: From perfect competition to monopoly - how structure shapes behaviour.
final_note: Structure shapes pricing power and incentives to innovate.

concepts.def: Many small firms, identical product, free entry.
Few large firms dominating the market.
Price equals marginal cost - no waste.

walkthroughs.body_html: Structures span perfect competition (price takers, normal profit) to monopoly (price maker, supernormal profit). Most real markets sit between as monopolistic competition or oligopoly.
Pricing power rises with barriers and concentration. Perfect competitors take the market price; monopolists choose the profit-maximising point on the demand curve.
Perfect competition delivers allocative and productive efficiency in theory. Monopoly produces less and charges more - but may invest more in R&D thanks to retained supernormal profit.
